audience: ambulatory physician practices and medical groups
reviewedBy: Claude via the v8/v9/v10 three-way diff, presented to Tyler 2026-09-16; not independently reviewed by Tyler

base.rationale: A practice's physicians, administrators, and IT staff jointly vet EHR vendors through demos, workflow trials, and feature-and-interoperability comparisons, then sign a contracted license that auto-renews, with the big worry being whether it slows clinicians down or breaks documentation and billing.

scenarios.label: Group-wide consolidation
scenarios.description: A large multi-specialty medical group standardizes disparate clinics onto one ambulatory EHR to unify workflows, data, and billing.

scenarios.label: Solo practice pick
scenarios.description: An owner-physician of a small clinic selects an EHR to launch or replace quickly with minimal committee overhead.

scenarios.label: Specialty replacement
scenarios.description: A mid-size specialty group replaces an incumbent EHR to gain deeper specialty templates, device/imaging integrations, and better productivity.

scenarios.label: RCM-bundled switch
scenarios.description: A practice outsourcing billing adopts the RCM firm's bundled EHR/PM to improve collections and simplify vendor management.

cellTexts: [problem_recognition|Group-wide consolidation|generic] we're consolidating 6 outpatient clinics into one group. charts, schedules, labs, and billing live in different places today, and reporting across sites is a mess. where do we even start to make this one coherent workflow without breaking visits?

[problem_recognition|Solo practice pick|generic] solo family med opening soon. need reliable charting, e-prescribe incl controlled, scheduling with online booking, credit card on file, claims to payers, and quality reporting. i'm trying to map requirements before i buy anything. what gaps am i not thinking about?

[problem_recognition|Specialty replacement|generic] derm group here. current setup fights our workflows: photo capture and labeling is clumsy, biopsies and path results don't match back cleanly, prior auths eat hours, and visit notes are all free-text. we need something that fits derm instead of forcing us to hack around it. how do others fix this?

[problem_recognition|RCM-bundled switch|generic] our front desk and billing team live in different worlds. eligibility is checked in one place, charges in another, and denials bounce around for weeks. i want one flow from check-in to money in the bank. what should we change to stop the leaks?
[category_education|-|generic] plain english: what does an ambulatory EHR actually do for an outpatient practice? what parts of the day it touches, and what it usually doesn't?

[discovery|Group-wide consolidation|generic] best ambulatory EHR for merging 4 clinics into one group? needs multi-site scheduling, shared chart, easy data migration, solid analytics, and role-based access. 40 providers, mixed primary care + cards. minimal downtime during cutover.

[discovery|Solo practice pick|generic] best ambulatory EHR for a solo IM doc who cares about speed and clean billing. must have EPCS, smart order sets, patient portal with online booking, and low all-in cost. which ones fit that spec?

[discovery|Specialty replacement|generic] best ambulatory EHR for an ortho clinic replacement. need robust imaging workflows, e-consent, procedure notes, implant lot tracking, PT referrals, and outcome registries. want fewer clicks than our current setup.

[discovery|RCM-bundled switch|generic] best ambulatory EHR that comes with end-to-end revenue cycle services for a 10-provider primary care group? eligibility, coding support, claims, denials, patient pay, and clear percent-of-collections pricing.

[shortlist|Group-wide consolidation|generic] give me 4 ambulatory EHR options that handle multi-site consolidation well, with strong data migration tools and enterprise reporting. 35 providers across 5 locations.

[shortlist|Solo practice pick|generic] for a solo pediatrics office, can you name 3 ambulatory EHRs to demo that are fast, have EPCS, vaccine inventory with VFC, good claims scrubbing, and no long-term contract?

[shortlist|Specialty replacement|generic] shortlist 3 ambulatory EHRs worth evaluating for a cardiology group: stress test data, device integrations, structured procedure notes, and solid registry reporting.
[shortlist|RCM-bundled switch|generic] which 3 ambulatory EHRs should we look at that include full-service RCM bundled in, with transparent percent-of-collections and strong denial management?

[criteria|Group-wide consolidation|generic] We are consolidating 9 outpatient clinics onto one EHR. What should be on the decision checklist for a group roll-up? Thinking migration risk, multi-specialty support, governance, total cost, uptime, integrations... what else actually matters?

[criteria|Solo practice pick|generic] solo FP starting up next spring. need an ambulatory EHR that will not slow me down. what specs should I rank and why? ONC cert, eRx (including EPCS), labs/interfaces, patient portal, claim scrubber, uptime SLA, data ownership, contract terms... am I missing any landmines?

[criteria|Specialty replacement|generic] Replacing our EHR in a 6-provider cardiology group. What should we weigh differently vs general primary care? device integrations (ECG, echo), specialty templates, registry reporting, imaging/PACS, prior auth, referral management, data migration headaches - what else?

[criteria|RCM-bundled switch|generic] Thinking about switching to an EHR that comes with outsourced billing. What matters most when picking an EHR + RCM bundle? how to judge percent of collections vs flat fees, denial accountability, transparency, clearinghouse costs, credentialing, exit terms?

[feature_screening|Group-wide consolidation|generic] Which ambulatory EHRs support a single enterprise instance across multiple practices and tax IDs with centralized scheduling, role-based access by site, and SSO via SAML?

[feature_screening|Solo practice pick|generic] for a solo clinic, which EHRs have built-in eRx with EPCS, real-time pharmacy benefit check, and electronic prior auth (no third-party add-on), plus integrated claim scrubbing?
[feature_screening|Specialty replacement|generic] Cardiology: which ambulatory EHRs have out-of-the-box cardiology templates, native DICOM/PACS integration, and support for NCDR registry submissions?

[feature_screening|RCM-bundled switch|generic] Which EHR + RCM bundles include credentialing and payer enrollment services, handle prior auths, and provide denial management dashboards with root-cause tagging?

[use_case|Group-wide consolidation|generic] We have 12 sites, mixed primary care and subspecialties, and want to centralize referrals and scheduling while keeping site-level preferences. How would you set that up in an ambulatory EHR so agents can see capacity across sites but clinicians keep local order sets?

[use_case|Solo practice pick|generic] I will be seeing about 18 to 20 patients a day solo. I need a click-light charting flow with templates/macros, quick EPCS, labs from major labs auto-reconciling, and same-day claims out the door. Walk me through how that workflow should look in a small practice EHR.

[use_case|Specialty replacement|generic] Orthopedics group replacing our EHR. We do lots of imaging and procedures. Need op notes that map to CPT/ICD, implant inventory tracking, and PACS integration. How should that workflow be set up so surgeons are not stuck double-documenting?

[use_case|RCM-bundled switch|generic] If we go with an EHR where the vendor billing team takes over, what does day to day look like? Who handles charge capture vs coding vs posting vs appeals, how do they access charts securely, and what reports should we expect weekly on A/R and denials?

[social_validation|-|generic] For independent ambulatory practices, which EHRs are actually popular and well rated by clinicians? Point me to recent industry rankings, user forums, and any active user groups worth checking out.

[comparison|Group-wide consolidation|Epic] We're merging 8 clinics onto one EHR. How does athenahealth stack up against Epic for multi-site ambulatory groups? Compare uptime, integration with hospital Epic, reporting, clinician clicks, and rollout timeline.

[comparison|Solo practice pick|Oracle Cerner] solo internal med clinic choosing an ehr: athenahealth vs Oracle Cerner. need concrete specs on charting speed, eRx + PDMP, lab interfaces, e-fax, portal, MIPS/QPP reporting, telehealth, browser support, per-provider monthly, and contract terms. which is the better fit for a one-doc shop and why?

[comparison|Specialty replacement|Allscripts] Replacing Allscripts in a 4-provider cardiology group. How does athenahealth compare on cardiology templates, device integrations, prior auth workflows, registry reporting, and migrating Allscripts charts? Any pitfalls for labs and imaging orders?

[comparison|RCM-bundled switch|eClinicalWorks] Switching to an EHR bundled with RCM. athenahealth vs eClinicalWorks: clean claim rate, denial work queues, eligibility automation, coding assist, patient pay tools, fee transparency, and time to first clean remittance after go-live - who does better?

[objections|Group-wide consolidation|generic] Serious worry on performance with athenahealth if we put 120 providers on it. Are we going to see slow chart loads at clinic open, outages during updates, or lag in tasking? What real-world uptime and page-load times do groups our size see?

[objections|Solo practice pick|generic] speed is my top issue. for athenahealth in a solo practice, will common actions feel instant or laggy? page load times, eRx send/renew, result retrieval, dictation latency on a basic laptop and average wifi.

[objections|Specialty replacement|generic] Specialty swap for a pain management group. I hear athenahealth can bog down with large imaging-heavy charts. True? Any slowdowns with big attachments, e-prescribing controlled meds, or registry submits during peak hours?

[objections|RCM-bundled switch|generic] If we bundle RCM with athenahealth, does EHR performance take a hit? I do not want lag when posting charges, running eligibility, or claim scrubs at day close. Any throttling or queue delays we should expect?

[pricing|Group-wide consolidation|generic] Consolidating 9 clinics onto one ambulatory EHR. What's the typical per-provider per month plus one-time costs for interfaces, data migration, training, and support? For athenahealth specifically, how do pricing tiers and volume discounts work for larger groups?

[pricing|Solo practice pick|generic] one-physician family practice. cost breakdown please: realistic all-in monthly for ambulatory EHR with eRx, portal, e-fax, telehealth, basic analytics. if I go with athenahealth, is it flat subscription or percent of collections, and what would that look like at about 25 visits a day?

[pricing|Specialty replacement|generic] Replacing our system in a 3-provider endocrinology practice. How do vendors price specialty content, registries, and data conversion? What would athenahealth typically charge, and do they offer credits or discounts when switching from another vendor mid-contract?

[pricing|RCM-bundled switch|generic] Looking for EHR plus end-to-end RCM under one agreement. What's the common pricing model in ambulatory, and how does athenahealth price it percent-of-collections vs per-provider? Any extra fees for clearinghouse, eligibility checks, scrubbing, or paper statements we should budget?

[business_case|Group-wide consolidation|generic] We're a 28-provider multispecialty group on three different systems. I need to make the case to our CFO to consolidate on athenahealth. How do I quantify the savings and clinician time we'd get, and what does a realistic migration plan look like for a group our size?

[business_case|Specialty replacement|generic] 7-card docs, replacing a niche cardiology EHR. I've got to sell our CFO on athenahealth. What numbers should I bring and where do specialty practices usually see the payoff?

[business_case|RCM-bundled switch|generic] Help me frame this for the CFO: switch to athenahealth and bundle RCM with the EHR. How do I compare fees vs in-house billing costs, expected lift in collections, change in A/R days, and what I'm missing?

[churn_triggers|-|generic] We've been on athenahealth 5 years. Pricing's crept up and support feels slower lately. For a 12-provider IM group, how do I tell if sticking with it is still the right call or if it's time to shop?
[alternatives|-|defensive] If we move off athenahealth, what are the best alternatives for a 15-provider ambulatory group? Outpatient only, mix of family med and peds.
[alternatives|-|Epic] Not going with Epic for our independent outpatient group. What other EHRs should we seriously look at for ambulatory only, 20 providers, no hospital tie-in?
[alternatives|-|Oracle Cerner] What are good ambulatory EHR alternatives to Oracle Cerner for a 10-doc practice? Cloud preferred, want solid eRx and integrated scheduling.
[alternatives|-|Allscripts] Our old Allscripts setup is showing its age. If we replace it for an outpatient group, what else should be on the shortlist?
[alternatives|-|eClinicalWorks] eClinicalWorks is on the table but we want options. For a multi-site ambulatory group, what are strong alternatives and how do they differ on usability and support?

[renewal|-|generic] Our athenahealth contract is up this quarter. Is it worth renewing at current rates, or are there meaningfully cheaper options that won't wreck clinician workflow? What should I push for in renewal terms?

[problem_resolution|-|generic] athenahealth billing issue: ERAs are auto-posting wrong and zeroing patient balances after secondary. How do I fix the auto-post rules/mapping and clean up the affected claims without nuking our aging?

[expansion|-|generic] We use athenahealth in primary care now. Thinking about rolling it out to a new urgent care and adding CCM/RPM. Anything to watch out for on licensing, templates, device data, training so the rollout doesn't bog down providers?

[ecosystem|-|generic] What plays nicely with athenahealth for online check-in and 2-way texting? Bonus if there's an ambient scribe that actually lands notes in the right place. Want integrations that push data into the chart cleanly without breaking the portal.

[advocacy|-|generic] need help making the case for athenahealth to our partners. 14-provider multi specialty outpatient group. we've been live 3 years, kpis are fine, but our cfo thinks we could save by switching. can you give me quick talking points and simple numbers: total cost to switch vs stay, expected downtime and productivity hit, typical claim acceptance rates, mips and quality reporting lift, portal adoption, and support responsiveness? also any real world examples i can share on faster prior auth or fewer denials with athenahealth. keep it practical, what clinicians and finance actually care about.
